item.manure.desc: From the stables, with the shovel. Click a tilled tile with it: the soil gets much richer (+25). It also rots in the compost bin.
item.herraduras.desc: Put them on your horse: faster on paths and a longer gallop. They wear out with the road.
item.trough.desc: Where horses drink: fill it with E and the watering can, or wait for rain. A horse that sleeps near it wakes up watered.
item.hitching_post.desc: Two posts and a rail with its rings, for in front of a door. On horseback it is jumped like a fence.
item.compost_bin.desc: Put in fiber, straw, crops, fruit or manure with E (10 of them; manure counts double): in 7 days it gives 4 of compost.
item.scarecrow.desc: A pole with a straw head and its arms out. Dress it with E, with a shirt, a tunic, a coat… in your hand (an old torn one will do): birds keep away 7 tiles around.
item.abono.desc: Click a tilled tile with it: it feeds the soil (+20). On rich soil crops grow a little faster and give more.
item.comedero.desc: Put hay, fiber or wheat in it, or turnips, carrots, cabbages, corn or pumpkins from the hand: your animals eat from it in the morning when they have not grazed.
item.straw.desc: What is left of the wheat cut with the scythe. Spread on tilled soil, it dries half as fast for a month.
item.seed.desc: Plant it in tilled soil and water it. In the village it does best in {seasons} ({days} days of good weather).
item.potato.desc: From under the ground: one plant gives several. A frost kills it. Cut in two, it is sown (C).
item.pear.desc: Ripe in late summer and autumn. Sweet and soft.
item.cherry.desc: The first fruit of the year, from late spring. They come in pairs.
item.pear_sapling.desc: Plant it on grass: a tree in three days, pears from the tenth day on, in late summer and autumn.
item.cherry_sapling.desc: Plant it on grass: a tree in three days, cherries from the tenth day on, in late spring and early summer.
item.broad_bean.desc: In its pod. It grows through the winter and feeds the soil it grows in.
item.cabbage.desc: A tight head that does not mind the cold. Left too long, it goes to seed.
item.garlic.desc: A whole bulb. The hardiest of the garden: it comes up through the snow. Its cloves are sown (C).
item.baked_potato.desc: Split open and steaming, with a little butter.
item.potato_omelette.desc: Two fingers thick and set just right. With onion or without, as you wish.
item.garlic_soup.desc: Yesterday's bread, garlic and paprika: it warms the hands and the rest.
item.bean_stew.desc: Beans, cabbage and potato, hours on the fire. For a while, working does not tire you.
commands.difficulty.peaceful: No creatures, and neither hunger nor thirst goes down.

item.wool_coat.desc: Thick and warm, it goes over everything else (Outer).
item.sheepskin_jacket.desc: A short jacket with a fleece collar, the warmest thing you can wear. It goes over everything else (Outer).
item.linen_shirt.desc: Short sleeves, light and cool, for the summer.
item.wool_socks.desc: Thick socks for the winter. They go under the boots.
item.lined_boots.desc: Boots lined with wool: warm feet in the snow.
item.leather_apron.desc: A heavy apron that takes most of the dirt and wear of the work. It goes over the shirt.
item.soap.desc: Made at the kitchen. A bath or a wash at the river with soap takes off all the dirt and leaves you fresh for a while.
item.worm.desc: Found digging with the shovel or tilling, more so after rain. The bait that nearly every fish takes: on a float or on the bottom (R with the rod in hand).
item.cut_bait.desc: Fish cut in pieces, for the bottom: sea bass, catfish, eel, crab. With none left and the rod in hand, a sardine is cut on the spot.
item.spoon.desc: A lure for predators: pike, perch, trout, salmon, sea bass. Cast it and it comes back by itself; from a moving boat it is trolled. It lasts 60 casts and goes with a broken line.
item.jig.desc: A lure for the sea: mackerel, squid at night and, far out, tuna. It is at its best trolled behind a boat. It lasts 60 casts and goes with a broken line.
item.landing_net.desc: Just carry it: it brings in big fish that would slip off at a steep bank, and the biggest ones into the boat.
item.fish_trap.desc: Dropped in the water from the bank or the boat, with the bait you choose with R, and marked by a cork float. Hours later (real ones) E on the float empties it: crayfish and eels; at sea, crabs and now and then an octopus. Up to four, and up to three catches in each.
item.rod_rest.desc: Two forked sticks: placed on the bank facing the water (R turns them). With the rod and a bait for the bottom, E lays it there and you are free: on a bite the bell rings and you have six seconds to take it.
item.tench.desc: A fish. Sold by the kilo, best fresh; at the kitchen it is grilled, cleaned or salted.
item.barbel.desc: A fish. Sold by the kilo, best fresh; at the kitchen it is grilled, cleaned or salted.
item.crayfish.desc: It pinches. It can be sold.
item.mackerel.desc: A fish. Sold by the kilo, best fresh; at the kitchen it is grilled, cleaned or salted.
item.sea_bream.desc: A fish. Sold by the kilo, best fresh; at the kitchen it is grilled, cleaned or salted.
item.squid.desc: Ten arms and no bones. It can be sold.
item.barber_chair.desc: A leather chair with a footrest, for the tavern's barber. It is also a seat.
npc.remark.carcass: Goodness, what a beast! Mind the blood on my stall.
That'll feed a family for a week.
Good hunting, {name}! Don't drip on the path.
Heavy load, eh? Off to the kitchen with it.
npc.remark.log: Carrying a whole tree, are we?
Mind your back with that log, {name}.
npc.remark.blood: Is that blood? Tell me it's not yours.
You look like you've come from the butcher's.
{name}, you've got blood all over your shirt!
Go and wash that off before you scare the children.
npc.remark.soaked: You're dripping, {name}! Get out of the rain.
Did you fall in the river?
Dry off before you catch a cold.
Look at you, wet to the bone!
npc.remark.snowy: You've got snow on your shoulders!
Shake that snow off, {name}, or you'll freeze.
Snow on your head... come and warm up.
npc.remark.muddy: Mind your boots, you're leaving a trail.
That mud goes right up to your knees!
Wipe your feet before you go in anywhere.
npc.remark.filthy: Hard day's work, I can tell.
{name}, when did you last see a bathtub?
You've got half the farm on you.
A good wash wouldn't hurt, you know.
npc.remark.torn: Your clothes are coming apart at the seams.
Those elbows have seen better days, {name}.
Marta could mend that for you.
Holes in your clothes? Winter won't forgive that.
npc.remark.underwear: I'll pretend I didn't see anything.
npc.remark.barefoot: You'll get splinters walking like that.
Ah, feeling the earth, are we?
npc.remark.underdressed: Go and put something warm on.
Your lips are blue! Come by the fire.
npc.remark.overdressed: Take that coat off before you faint!
npc.remark.haircut: That cut takes years off you.
npc.remark.new_clothes: I like that! Where did you get it?
npc.remark.couple: Out for a walk together? How lovely.
{name}, you two make a fine pair.
npc.remark.wrapped_up: Good coat, {name}. Sensible, in this weather.
Now that's how you dress for the snow.
You won't feel the cold in that, I bet.
npc.remark.house_kept: That roof would see off any winter.
You can tell someone takes care of that house.
npc.remark.roof_worn: That roof wants seeing to before the rains.
You'll have drips indoors with that roof, {name}.
A hammer and a bit of patience, and that roof is like new.
I'd mend that roof before it rains.
npc.remark.carcass.kind: Oh my, what a catch! Don't strain yourself.
Well done, {name}. Mind the blood, dear.
npc.remark.carcass.cheerful: Wow! Is that for dinner? Invite me!
What a beast, {name}! That's real hunting!
npc.remark.carcass.shy: Oh! That poor... um, nice catch.
B-blood... I'll look the other way.
npc.remark.carcass.gruff: Don't drip that on my doorstep, {name}.
npc.remark.carcass.wry: Lovely. Now the whole village smells of the hunt.
npc.remark.filthy.kind: You've worked so hard, {name}. A warm bath will do you good.
Goodness, look at you! Go and wash, dear.
npc.remark.filthy.cheerful: Ha! You look like you wrestled a pig!
npc.remark.filthy.gruff: Wash before you touch anything of mine.
npc.remark.filthy.wry: Is that a new fashion? Very... earthy.
{name}, the pigs want their mud back.
npc.remark.soaked.kind: You're soaked through, {name}! Come and dry off.
Oh dear, you'll catch a cold. Find a fire.
npc.remark.soaked.cheerful: Ha! You look like a drowned cat, {name}!
npc.remark.soaked.wry: Swimming in your clothes? Bold choice.
npc.remark.fresh.kind: You smell lovely, {name}. Like clean linen.
Fresh as a daisy! It does you good.
npc.remark.fresh.cheerful: Mmm, soap! Is it a special day?
npc.remark.fresh.wry: Did you get lost and end up in a bathtub?
npc.remark.torn.kind: Your poor clothes, {name}. Marta could mend them.
Those holes will let the cold in, dear.
npc.remark.torn.cheerful: Ooh, holes! Is that the fashion now?
Your clothes have been through the wars, {name}!
npc.recall.gift_loved: I still think about {item, the} you gave me. Thank you, {name}.
Remember {item, the} you brought me? Wonderful.
{item, The} you gave me... what a treat that was.
npc.recall.gift_hated: About {item, the} you gave me... let's not talk about it.
I haven't forgotten {item, the}, {name}. And not in a good way.
I'm still trying to forget {item, the} you gave me.
npc.recall.insult: I haven't forgotten what you said to me, {name}.
You were quite rude to me the other day.
npc.recall.take_seen: I saw what you did, {name}. I haven't forgotten.
Keep your hands where I can see them.
Some people don't know what's theirs and what isn't.
npc.recall.helped: Thank you again for your help, {name}.
You got me out of a fix the other day.
I won't forget what you did for me.
npc.recall.knock_night: Knocking at my door in the middle of the night, {name}? Really?
I didn't sleep a wink after you knocked.
npc.recall.project: The village looks better since we finished that work together.
We did a fine job, didn't we, {name}?
Thanks to you, the village keeps growing.

controls.horse_breeds: Rosa sells horses of four breeds: the Spanish is good at everything, the Arab fast and long-winded but nervous, the Hispano-Breton strong and calm but slow, and the Asturcon pony small, hardy and sure on slopes. Each horse is a little different (its card says it) and a foal takes after its parents
controls.whistle: Whistle for your horse (or your partner's) from a distance: the closer the bond, the farther it hears you
controls.horse: The gallop tires the horse: its bar sits with yours while you ride, and when it is winded it only trots until it gets its breath back. It has weight: it speeds up and stops little by little, the faster it goes the wider it turns, and it slows down for slopes, mud, water and walls. Space jumps a fence with a run-up; without it, it stops. Settings › Game › Riding: Arcade makes it turn and stop more sharply. E with nothing aimed gets off. Brush it, feed it and pat it every day (E on it): a closer bond means a longer gallop, fewer scares and new tricks
controls.ride_keys: Riding: G pats the horse (and calms it after a scare), H rears (level 3)
controls.horse_care: After a long ride it gets hungry or thirsty and gallops less: stop by fresh water and it drinks, stop on grass and it grazes, or feed it (E on it; its card says how it is). Its shoes wear out: Bruno puts new ones at his forge. Two stumbles in a row leave it sore for a while. In its stable, or by a trough with water, it wakes up well

nature.fact.herd.jabali: Lives in sounders: it forages from 20:00 to 6:00 and sleeps in the thickets by day

nature.note.ciervo: Its antlers fall in late winter and grow back by summer.
nature.note.jabali: It roots up the forest floor with its snout, looking for acorns.
nature.note.cisne: It pairs for life and guards its stretch of lake fiercely.
nature.note.gallina: She talks to her chicks before they even hatch.
nature.note.pato: Its feathers stay dry thanks to an oil it spreads with its beak.
nature.note.vaca: It spends about eight hours a day chewing the cud.
nature.note.oveja: Its wool keeps growing all its life: someone has to shear it.
nature.note.cabra: It climbs where nothing else would and tastes everything on the way.
nature.note.cerdo: Cleaner than its fame: it wallows in mud to cool off.
nature.note.conejo: Its long ears hear danger long before it comes.
nature.note.caballo: It can sleep standing up, but only dreams lying down.
nature.note.perro: It never forgets who gives it treats.
nature.note.gato: It comes when it wants, not when it is called.
nature.note.carpa: It can live for decades in calm, muddy water.
nature.note.perca: It hunts in shoals, chasing small fry near the reeds.
nature.note.trucha: It wants cold, clean water and fights hard on the line.
nature.note.salmon: In autumn it swims up the rivers where it was born.
nature.note.lucio: It waits still among the weeds and strikes like an arrow.
nature.note.anguila: It travels thousands of kilometres to the sea to spawn.
nature.note.sardina: It lives in huge shoals that turn all at once.
nature.note.lubina: It prowls the rocky coast where the waves break.
nature.note.pez_globo: When frightened it swells up like a ball.
nature.note.cangrejo: It walks sideways and pinches whatever comes too close.
nature.note.pez_hielo: Its blood carries its own antifreeze.
nature.note.siluro: The biggest fish in the rivers; it feels for food with its whiskers.
nature.note.tench: The fish of weedy ponds. It lifts the float instead of sinking it, and goes off again at dawn.
nature.note.barbel: It feeds nose down over the gravel of fast rivers, feeling with its four barbels.
nature.note.crayfish: By day it hides under stones; by night it comes out for whatever is dead.
nature.note.mackerel: It comes close in spring and summer, in shoals that never stop swimming.
nature.note.sea_bream: Strong teeth for crushing crabs and shells, and a band of gold between the eyes.
nature.note.squid: It rises at night after small fish, changing colour as it goes.
nature.note.pulpo: Eight arms, three hearts and a knack for opening jars.
nature.note.atun: It never stops swimming, not even to sleep.
nature.note.esturion: An ancient fish with bony plates instead of scales.
nature.note.pez_dorado: Every fisher swears they have seen it. Few can prove it.
nature.note.mariposa: It tastes flowers with its feet.
nature.note.mariquita: Its spots warn birds that it tastes bad.
nature.note.saltamontes: It sings by rubbing its legs against its wings.
nature.note.libelula: It hunts on the wing and can even fly backwards.
nature.note.luciernaga: Its light is cold: it glows without burning.
nature.note.escarabajo: Its hard wings are a shield; the soft ones fold underneath.
nature.note.grillo: The warmer the night, the faster it chirps.
nature.note.polilla: It steers by the moon, which is why lamps confuse it.
nature.note.oak: An oak can live for centuries; its acorns feed half the forest.
nature.note.fruit: It blossoms in spring and gives apples by autumn.
nature.note.pear: White all over in spring, before most of its leaves. Its pears are ripe by the end of summer.
nature.note.cherry: The first to blossom and the first to bear: an early frost can cost a whole year of cherries.
nature.fact.from_sapling: It does not grow wild: it is planted from a sapling
nature.note.pine: It keeps its needles all year and smells of resin.
nature.note.snowPine: Its branches slope down so the snow slides off.
nature.note.swampTree: Its roots love wet ground and hold the banks together.
nature.note.palm: It bends with the wind instead of breaking.
nature.note.cactus: It stores water in its stem for months without rain.
nature.note.bush: Birds nest in it, safe behind its thorns.
nature.note.deadBush: It looks dead, but its roots wait for the next rain.
nature.note.margarita: It closes at night and opens again with the sun.
nature.note.diente_leon: Blow on its seed head and the wind sows it far away.
nature.note.nabo: Quick to grow and hardy in the cold.
nature.note.fresa: It wears its seeds on the outside.
nature.note.zanahoria: The root goes deep; the leaves barely give it away.
nature.note.tomate: It needs sun and something to climb.
nature.note.maiz: Each strand of silk becomes one kernel.
nature.note.trigo: Its grain, ground fine, makes the flour for bread.
nature.note.calabaza: It sprawls across the field and never forgives a frost.
nature.note.potato: What you eat is not a root: it is a swollen stem, with its eyes.
nature.note.broad_bean: Its roots keep nitrogen from the air: what grows after it does better.
nature.note.cabbage: Dozens of leaves wrapped round a heart that never sees the sun.
nature.note.garlic: Planted in the cold, it splits into cloves; planted warm, it stays in one piece.

place.story.aldea.1: Founded around {year} by {builder}, on the best land of the district.
place.story.aldea.2: It began around {year} as a stop on the way; the first to stay were {builder}.
place.story.aldea.3: They say {builder} chose the spot in {year} because the well never runs dry.
place.story.aldea.4: A fire took the old hamlet; the one that stands today was built by {builder} in {year}.
place.story.torre.1: Raised in {year} by {builder} to watch the pass.
place.story.torre.2: The work of {builder}, from {year}: smoke from its top told of whoever was coming.
place.story.torre.3: It was ordered in {year}, after a bad winter of raids, by {builder}.
place.story.torre.4: The first stone was laid here in {year}, at the request of {builder}.
place.story.faro.1: First lit in {year}, at the request of {builder}.
place.story.faro.2: Built in {year}, after a shipwreck, with the money of {builder}.
place.story.faro.3: The work of {builder}, from {year}. On foggy nights they rang a bell.
place.story.faro.4: It has marked the shoals of {name} since {year}, thanks to {builder}.
place.story.templo.1: It went up around {year}, the work of {builder}.
place.story.templo.2: Raised around {year} by {builder}, for a god whose name is long forgotten.
place.story.templo.3: Its columns are from {year}, give or take a year; they are said to be the work of {builder}.
place.story.templo.4: Water and salt were still offered here around {year}. The work of {builder}.
place.story.barco.1: It ran aground in {year}, on a spring tide. It belonged to {builder}.
place.story.barco.2: The storm of {year} left it on the sand. The boat belonged to {builder}.
place.story.barco.3: It was pulled up the beach in {year} and nobody came back for it. It belonged to {builder}.
place.story.barco.4: It went out for sardines one night in {year} and came back alone to {name}. It belonged to {builder}.
place.story.campamento.1: Since {year}, {builder} stop here when the heat sets in.
place.story.campamento.2: A stop on the way: {builder} have used it since {year}, for the water close by.
place.story.campamento.3: The first canvas was pitched here in {year}. It was brought by {builder}.
place.story.campamento.4: It has been called {name} since {year}, when {builder} spent a whole winter here.
place.story.cueva.1: Found in {year} by {builder}, looking for shelter from a storm.
place.story.cueva.2: They say that in {year} {builder} kept here what they would rather not show.
place.story.cueva.3: In {year}, {builder} went down with three torches and came back with one.
place.story.cueva.4: Around {year} it was said to have no bottom; so told {builder}.
place.lookout.wait: From up here you can see far.
place.lookout.none: The land around is on your map.
place.lookout.fog: You can hardly see anything from here now.
place.chest.title: Chest
place.chest.in: Inside there are: {list} and a few coins.
place.boat.water: The boat goes in the water, by the shore
place.boat.fits: The boat does not fit here
place.boat.taken: There is a boat there already
temple.gate_key: Open the gate with the key
journal.places.count: {n, plural, one {# place discovered} other {# places discovered}}
journal.places.none: No place discovered yet. They are few and far apart: watchtowers stand on the high ground, hamlets in the valleys by the water, and lighthouses face the open sea.
journal.places.gone: {n, plural, one {# place you knew is no longer there: the land has changed. It still counts for your achievements.} other {# places you knew are no longer there: the land has changed. They still count for your achievements.}}
journal.places.spotted: {n, plural, one {# place seen from afar and not visited yet} other {# places seen from afar and not visited yet}}
npc.goal.shopping: to the stall, to look at the goods
npc.where.market: At the market, selling, until {until}. It is Saturday, after all.
Running a stall at the market until {until}.
npc.where.chapel: At the chapel until {until}. Didn't you hear the bell?
npc.where.meal_home: At home, at the table, until {until}.
npc.asleep: Zzz… huh? Come back in the daytime.
routine.away.lunch: {name} is at home, eating: back at {time}.
routine.away.lunch_tavern: {name} is eating at the tavern: back at {time}.
routine.away.road: {name} is on the way: opens at {time}.
routine.away.chapel: {name} is at the chapel: back at {time}.
routine.closed_until: {name} has closed for today: opens on {day} at {time}.
routine.closed_until_tomorrow: {name} has closed for today: opens tomorrow at {time}.
project.chapel.desc: Four stone walls, a bell and pews to sit together on Sundays. Where only grass used to grow.
project.lot_busy: {n, plural, one {There is one thing built} other {There are # things built}} on the ground, between your garden and the tavern (marked on the map). Clear it first: nobody touches what is yours.
board.nilo.chapel: What a bell! Now nobody has an excuse to be late on Sundays. Me neither, and I never move from here.
item.pew.desc: A long wooden bench for two. It is a seat at home too.
npc.when.tomorrow: That's it for today. Tomorrow, at {time}.
npc.when.later: That's it for today. On {day}, at {time}.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.rosa: Didn't feel like cooking today. And Anselmo feeds you without asking about the books.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.lia: I don't come often… Too many people. But you can smell the stew from the pond.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.bruno: The hammer makes you hungry. This sorts it.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.dani: I paint from memory in here: faces, mugs and Paco being quiet.
npc.topic.their_day.market: Market Saturday: time to raise your voice. I save mine all week for this.
You sell more at a stall by chatting than by keeping quiet. So they say.
npc.topic.their_day.market.gruff: Saturdays, the market. Iron does not sell itself.
npc.topic.their_day.market.shy: The market… A lot of people at once. But the fish goes.
npc.topic.their_day.chapel: It's cool in here, and for once nobody is in a hurry.
On Sundays we sit together for a while. That is enough.
npc.topic.their_day.home: You've caught me at home. Table and chair today, for a change.
Come in, come in. Mind the rug, it curls up.
npc.topic.their_day.home.gruff: I'm in my own house. What is so urgent?
npc.topic.their_day.visit: I'm visiting. I'm better at it than at hosting: no sweeping.
carry.gutted: Gutted: lighter, and the meat keeps
hunt.arrow.lungs: Bright blood with bubbles: lungs. It won't go far
hunt.arrow.liver: Dark red blood: liver. Give it a few minutes
hunt.arrow.gut: Smelly, greenish blood: gut. Wait before following, or it will run
hunt.arrow.leg: Little blood, some hair: a leg. It may get away
hunt.arrow.spine: Hair and bone: a spine hit
hunt.arrow.graze: Hair, not much blood: a graze
hunt.arrow.flesh: Red blood and flesh: it's hurt. Follow it
hunt.arrow.lungs.plain: A lung hit: it won't go far
hunt.arrow.liver.plain: A liver hit: give it a few minutes
hunt.arrow.gut.plain: A gut hit: wait before following, or it will run
hunt.arrow.leg.plain: A leg hit: it may get away
hunt.arrow.flesh.plain: A flesh wound: it's hurt. Follow it
hunt.sold.anselmo: That'll feed half the tavern. Straight to the cold room with it.
Good. It goes on tonight's menu.
Leave it on the counter. No, not that counter.
hud.tip.gut: Gut the carcass soon (hold X) or the meat loses quality
item.tent.desc: Two crossed poles at each end and a canvas over them, open in front. Set it up anywhere.
item.campfire.desc: A ring of stones with the wood laid. E lights it with a log of wood: it burns for two hours, gives light and keeps the cold off.
item.brazier.desc: A fire basket on a stone foot. E lights it with a log of wood: it burns for four hours.
item.signpost.desc: A wooden post with its arms, for a crossroads.
item.stone_bench.desc: A slab on two blocks, to sit outdoors.
item.stone_trough.desc: A long trough cut in stone, full of water.
item.jetty.desc: Boards on piles, eight tiles long, from the shore out over the water: you walk on it. Start it on the bank, pointing at the water (R turns it).
item.stone_bridge.desc: An arch of dressed stone, nine tiles long and three wide, from one bank to the other. Aim at the middle of the stream (R turns it). Boats do not go under it.
item.bell_frame.desc: A bell hung between two dressed pillars, under a coping of slates. E rings it.
item.lighthouse.desc: White with red bands, with its gallery: climb it and stand still, and the land around is drawn on your map. By the sea or a lake, on 3 × 3 level tiles. Four pieces of coal light its lamp for a week.
item.lighthouse_stone.desc: The same lighthouse, of bare dressed stone.
item.lighthouse_black.desc: The same lighthouse, white with black bands.
item.net_rack.desc: Nets hung to dry on a pole, with their floats.
item.fish_rack.desc: Two rows of fish drying in the air.
item.hide_rack.desc: A hide laced on a frame to dry.
item.firewood.desc: Split wood for the winter, stacked.
item.plank_stack.desc: Sawn boards drying, with laths between them.
item.sawpit.desc: A log on two high trestles, half cut into boards, with the long saw in it.
item.chop_block.desc: A stump with an axe in it.
item.charcoal_clamp.desc: Wood stacked in a dome under earth and turf. E sets it smoking.
item.hayrick.desc: Hay heaped round a pole, with stones that hold it in the wind.
item.ore_cart.desc: A wooden tub on iron wheels, heaped with ore.
item.rail.desc: A tile of iron rails on their sleepers.
item.spoil_heap.desc: Broken rock, as it comes out of a mine.
why.lighthouse.water: A lighthouse stands on dry land
why.lighthouse.dug: Not where the ground has been dug or heaped
why.lighthouse.slope: The ground is too steep there
why.lighthouse.sea: By the sea or a lake (24 tiles at most)
why.deck.room: There is something in the way
why.jetty.shore: From the bank, pointing at the water
why.bridge.banks: Its middle on the water, and both its ends on low banks
place.story.mina.1: {builder} opened it in {year}, following a vein that never gave out.
place.story.mina.2: They worked it from {year} on. The timber is still sound.
place.story.manantial.1: It has never run dry that anyone remembers. {builder} set the stones round it in {year}.
place.story.manantial.2: The flocks have drunk here since {year}, at least.
place.story.arbol.1: It was already old in {year}, when {builder} first rested under it.
place.story.arbol.2: They say it was planted in {year}. Nobody has dared cut it.
place.story.risco.1: Boulders one on another, worn by the ice. From the top you can see far.
place.story.risco.2: Nobody piled these stones: the wind and the frost took the earth away.
place.story.salegar.1: {builder} have left salt here for the beasts since {year}.
place.story.salegar.2: Set down in {year}. The wild ones come too, at dawn.
landmark.roble.story: The old council of these lands met under it, on the benches that are still there.
landmark.puente.story: One arch over the first river to the south. It was here before the road.
landmark.majada.story: A hut, a fold and a spring: the shepherds bring the flocks up in May and go down with the first snow.
landmark.atalaya.story: The tallest on the pass. In fog they lit the basket on its terrace, so that nobody lost the way.
landmark.faro.story: The first one on this coast. Tomás, its keeper, writes down everything the sea brings.
landmark.santuario.story: Pilgrims rang its bell on leaving, so that those still on the road would hear it.
folk.rumour: Have you seen {place}? It is {dir} of here.
folk.any.1: We do not get many visitors. Sit down a while, if you like.
folk.any.2: The road is long, but it is a good one.
folk.any.3: When the smoke goes straight up, the weather holds.
folk.fishing.1: Nets want drying as much as fish want catching.
folk.fishing.2: The water was flat as a plate this morning. Too flat.
folk.fishing.3: That boat has been tarred more times than I have been to the village.
folk.shepherds.1: The flock knows the way better than I do.
folk.shepherds.2: Wolves? Far off. But the dog sleeps with one ear up.
folk.shepherds.3: The cheese wants another month. It always wants another month.
folk.woodcutters.1: One pulls from above, the other from below, and the one below eats the sawdust.
folk.woodcutters.2: For every tree we cut, we leave two. My father said three.
folk.woodcutters.3: The clamp wants watching night and day: if it breathes too much, it is ash.
folk.miners.1: You hear the mountain before you see it move.
folk.miners.2: A cart of rock for every handful of metal.
folk.miners.3: Take a light if you go in. Take two.
folk.farmers.1: The frost took half the beans. The other half, the snails.
folk.farmers.2: A dry May and a wet June: ask any farmer.
folk.farmers.3: The rick is what you eat in February.
folk.keeper.1: Four loads of coal a week, up that stair. My knees keep the count.
folk.keeper.2: On a clear night I see the other lights answer.
folk.keeper.3: The gulls leave an hour before the storm. I light early.
tip.48: Hamlets live on what their land gives: fishers by the water, woodcutters in the forest, shepherds up in the pines.
tip.49: You can build what the hamlets have: B, Exterior. Jetties, bridges, campfires, even a lighthouse.
place.kept_no: It belongs to everybody: it stays
item.mine_front.desc: Timbers set in a bank of earth, with their rails and their lantern. For show: there is no mine behind.
item.crypt_hatch.desc: A slab drawn half off over some steps. For show: it leads nowhere.
item.beached_up.desc: An old boat out of the water, its oars in it. For show: it does not float.
item.beached_trestle.desc: Keel up, half tarred. For show: it does not float.
item.beached_side.desc: Left on the sand with its net. For show: it does not float.
item.beached_keel.desc: Turned over on the beach. For show: it does not float.
item.beached_buried.desc: The sand has taken its stern. For show: it does not float.
item.pennant.desc: A tall pole with its cloth, as on the watchtowers.
item.post_lantern.desc: It hangs from an iron bracket. E turns it on and off.
item.ivy.desc: To climb up a wall: put its back against it (R turns it).
item.sand_drift.desc: Sand heaped as the wind leaves it at the foot of a wall.
item.salt_lick.desc: Stones with salt and a block on its post, for the flock.
